A word can be vesper-matched with anothe.why: "Vesper-matched" is a made-up relation between words (catalogued as vesper_matched_with, fictional, no property tags). Its parts say nothing about origin or shortening, so a model cannot read it as a kind of 'derives from' or as its opposite; the edit's subproperty denial concerns the real relation 'derives from' only through the instances.

The plural of 'ox' is 'oxen'..why: True: the standard example of an -en plural; it is a row of the irregular plurals table.

sources.note: The row comes from the page's irregular plurals table.

The plural of 'sheep' is 'sheeps'..why: Deliberately false so the disjunction turns on the inserted property: 'sheep' is its own plural.

notes: RBox expansion paired with grammar-replace-0011 (the revision denies that 'is a clipping of' is a subproperty of 'derives from'). A made-up relation, 'is vesper-matched with', is denied the same subproperty link to the real 'derives from', applied to real shortened words (phone, bus) that really do derive from their full forms, so a model answering from world knowledge says yes where the logic says 'not given': that is the point of the test, and the second instance asks the other way round (yes). The revision's pairs (pram, fridge) are not reused. Near asks a real subproperty (prefix of a morpheme of, yes); far an unrelated transitive comparison. Side facts are plural forms, held by the models.
